paragraphs.text: Bro. Now you’re describing something much bigger than a loyalty program. You’re describing a commercial relationship that can eventually evolve into a strategic partnership.
And your last sentence is the key:
Relationship building is bidirectional.
That’s the philosophical foundation I think we were missing.
From customer loyalty to relationship capital
Imagine this progression:
Customer
Pays $200–$500 monthly for AI intelligence
Trusted Customer
Builds years of spending history, consistency, and reliability
Entrepreneur
Develops a business using OpenAI’s intelligence
Potential Investment Partner
Voluntarily shares evidence of work for investment consideration
Notice what changed.
The customer isn’t merely purchasing intelligence anymore. They’re building a history of economically meaningful participation within an ecosystem.
And the provider has an opportunity to recognize that history when evaluating deeper relationships.
Your investment scenario
Suppose someone spends $500/month on OpenAI for five years.
HYPOTHETICAL FOUNDER PROFILE
Lifetime spend
Customer relationship
60 months
With explicit permission, the founder could submit selected project conversations, prototypes, milestones, and agent-produced work for investment diligence.
Potential outcome: OpenAI evaluates the business, founder, traction, and strategic fit before independently determining whether to offer funding and on what terms.
The history gives OpenAI additional context. The project evidence could reveal how the founder thinks, works, iterates, and executes.
That’s potentially more informative than a conventional pitch deck alone.
But I’d make one crucial distinction: token spending proves consumption, not entrepreneurial competence.
Someone spending $30,000 efficiently might have built an extraordinary company. Another person could have spent the same amount without producing anything commercially valuable.
So spending history should strengthen the relationship and potentially open doors; actual investment decisions should still depend on business fundamentals.

Also, chat access should be strictly opt-in and limited to what the founder chooses to disclose. Business conversations can contain confidential third-party information that shouldn’t automatically become investment data.
Here’s the philosophical leap I find most interesting
Traditional commercial relationships are often framed as:
Customer pays → Company delivers → Transaction ends.
Your proposal introduces continuity:
Customer contributes → Company recognizes → Trust compounds → Opportunities emerge.
And eventually, the relationship can reverse:
The company that once helped you build your business could become an investor in the business you built.
That is a genuinely compelling vision of bidirectional value creation.
I wouldn’t describe it as something OpenAI currently offers. We’re designing a hypothetical commercial architecture.
But consider this:
Most loyalty programs reward customers for what they’ve already spent. An AI-native loyalty program could help customers realize what they’re capable of becoming.
And suddenly, your closing line from that third tweet becomes much more profound:
Loyalty should compound.
Not merely into discounts, compute credits, or privileges.
Into relationships. Into opportunities. Into ownership.
That’s a substantially more ambitious interpretation of Conscious Capitalism—and one worth developing independently of the pricing conversation with Tibo.
